text: Being a good dad isn't the big speeches. It's showing up, again and again, when it's boring and nobody's clapping. You do that. That's the whole game.
Your kids won't remember every word you said. They'll remember that you were THERE. And you always are. That's the flex.
A good dad raises kids who feel safe being honest with him. That's not luck, Jamar. That's years of you doing the quiet work.
The patience you show your kids on a hard day is a superpower disguised as a normal Tuesday.
You're teaching them how a man treats people just by being you in the room. No pressure. Okay, some pressure. You've got it.
Great dads don't raise perfect kids. They raise kids who know they're loved no matter what. You nailed that part.
Showing up to the thing after a long day when you're exhausted is love in its most unglamorous, most real form. That's you.
You listen to your kids like what they're saying matters. Because it does. And they'll carry that forever.
The world has enough fathers who were 'around.' You're one who is PRESENT. There's a difference and your kids can feel it.
A good dad apologizes when he's wrong. That teaches more than a hundred lectures. You model it. Rare, and huge.
You make your kids feel like the most interesting people in the room. Most adults never get that from anyone.
Dad of the year isn't a trophy, it's a daily decision. You keep choosing it. Quietly. Relentlessly. Respect.
The way your kids light up when you walk in? You earned that. Every bit of it.
You're raising humans who will be kind because they watched you be kind. That's a legacy, my guy.
Some days being a dad is just making sure everyone's fed, safe, and knows they matter. You did that today. That's a win. Log it.
You listen to understand, not to reply. That's rarer than you think, and people feel it the second they're around you.
A good listener makes people feel less alone just by paying attention. You do that without even trying.
You remember the small things people tell you. That's not a small thing. That's how people know they matter to you.
Most people are just waiting for their turn to talk. You actually hear them. That's a quiet kind of leadership.
You let silence sit instead of rushing to fill it. That's where the real stuff comes out. You get that.
People tell you things they don't tell anyone else. That's not an accident. That's trust you built by listening.
Being heard is one of the deepest human needs, and you hand it to people like it's nothing. It is not nothing.
You ask the second question, the one past the surface. That's where people feel truly seen. Keep doing that.
A great listener doesn't fix everything. Sometimes he just says 'that sounds hard' and means it. You've got that instinct.
You make room for people to be messy and real. That safety you create, people remember it for years.
Listening well is a form of respect, and you give it generously. That's character, plain and simple.
You hear what people DON'T say too. That's not magic, it's attention. And it's a gift to everyone around you.
Real power isn't volume. It's the calm guy everyone looks to when things get hard. That's you.
You don't have to announce your strength. People feel it when you walk in steady. That's the quiet power.
Powerful men lift others up instead of standing on them. That's the only kind of power worth having, and it's yours.
Strength under control is the whole thing. You've got force AND restraint. That combination moves rooms.
You lead without needing the title. People follow you because of who you are, not what's on your badge.
The most powerful thing a man can be is dependable. People build their lives around your word. That's power.
You stay solid when things shake. That steadiness gives everyone around you permission to breathe. Underrated superpower.
Power is making the people around you better and then letting them take the credit. You do this. I've seen it.
A powerful man knows when NOT to use his power. You've got that wisdom. Most don't.
You carry weight without complaining about it. That's not just strong, that's grown. There's a difference.
Confidence that doesn't need to put anyone down is the real thing. The room-shifting kind. That's you.
You're the guy who gets handed the hard thing because everyone knows you'll carry it. That trust IS power.
Leading with empathy isn't soft. It's the hardest, strongest way to lead, and you choose it every time.
You see the person before the problem. That's why people give you their best. They feel respected first.
Empathy is just imagination aimed at other people, and you've got it in spades. It's your edge, not your weakness.
The best leaders make people feel understood before they ask them for anything. You lead like that instinctively.
You can disagree with someone and still make them feel respected. That's a masterclass most people never learn.
Leading with empathy means carrying what others are going through without making it about you. You're built for that.
People work harder for a leader who sees them as human. You never forget the human part. That's your whole game.
Empathy under pressure is the real test, and you pass it when it counts. People would follow that anywhere.
You meet people where they are instead of where you wish they were. That patience changes lives. Quietly.
The strongest thing you do all day is understand someone you disagree with. That's leadership, and it's rare.
Kindness isn't the opposite of strength, it's proof of it. You prove it daily. Keep leading like that.
You make hard calls without making people feel small. That balance is the whole art. You've got it.
Go Pack. That's it. That's the whole affirmation. Red runs in the blood, and yours runs loud. 🐺
The Wolfpack doesn't travel in packs for safety. They travel in packs because together they're unstoppable. Sound familiar?
Red and white, through thick and thin. Good seasons, bad seasons, you're Pack for life. That's loyalty, and loyalty's your thing.
A wolf doesn't lose sleep over the opinions of sheep. Carry that energy into Monday. Go Pack.
NC State red looks good on you because confidence looks good on you. Coincidence? The data says no.
The Pack protects its own. You've always been that guy for your people. Howl if you hear me. 🐺
Win or lose, you show up for the Pack. That's not fandom, that's character wearing a jersey.
They'll never understand the Wolfpack until they ARE the Wolfpack. You get it in your bones. Go Pack.
Some people pick a team. You picked a Pack. There's a difference, and it's the difference that defines you.
Strength in numbers, loyalty to the end, and a little chaos for fun. That's the Pack. That's you. 🐺
Howl loud, lead the Pack, leave it better than you found it. That's the whole philosophy, honestly.
Red is a state of mind. Yours is permanently set to Wolfpack. Respect. Go Pack!
I threw a grape at Dave this morning. He wasn't thrilled. I had grape expectations for that friendship.
Chucked some Colby Jack into the trash. Yelled Kobe. Nailed it. Cheese and basketball, finally united.
Told the customs officer I had nothing to declare. He punched me. So now I declare noticeably less.
I'm reading a book about anti-gravity. Honestly? Impossible to put down.
I used to be a banker, but I lost interest. Get it? Please get it. I need this.
I only know 25 letters of the alphabet. I don't know why.
I named my printer Bob Marley. It's always jammin'.
Wanted to tell you a pizza joke but it's too cheesy. Also I ate it.
I'm on a whiskey diet. Lost three days already.
Broke my arm in two places. Doctor said stop going to those places.
The past, present, and future all walked into a bar. It was tense.
I'm great friends with all the electricians. We have wonderful current events.
I named my horse Mayo. And sometimes... Mayo neighs.
I don't trust stairs. They're always up to something.
Put my grades in the fridge. Now they're below C level.
I told my suitcase there's no vacation this year. Now I'm dealing with emotional baggage.
Two antennas got married. The wedding was mid, but the reception was excellent.
I threw a boomerang a few years ago. I now live in constant fear.
Wanna hear a construction joke? I'm still working on it.
The lunch soup was 8 dollars. That's a lotta broth-er.
Escalators never break. They just become stairs. Sorry for the convenience.
I got a job at the bakery. Turns out I really kneaded the dough.
I have a fear of speed bumps. But I'm slowly getting over it.
Refused the ceiling repair. It was completely over my head.
A guy walked into a bar. Ow. Just... ow.
I ordered a chicken and an egg online. I'll let you know which comes first.
Time flies like an arrow. Fruit flies like a banana. I've made peace with neither.
I stayed up all night wondering where the sun went. Then it dawned on me.
My calendar's days are numbered. All of them. Every single one.
Honey never spoils. They found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs, still edible. I still wouldn't.
A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance. I've filed paperwork to rename the sales team.
Octopuses have three hearts. Two stop when they swim, so they prefer to crawl. Deeply relatable.
Bananas are berries. Strawberries are not. Nothing means anything. Have a great day.
Wombat poop is cube-shaped. Nature invented dice and told nobody. I've said too much.
A shrimp's heart is in its head. So when a shrimp follows its heart, it's just... thinking.
There are more possible chess games than atoms in the observable universe. Dave still beat me in four moves.
Sea otters hold hands while sleeping so they don't drift apart. Our group chat can't agree on lunch.
Cows have best friends and get stressed when separated. Somebody put HR on this.
Scotland's national animal is the unicorn. Objectively the correct decision.
The guy who invented the frisbee was cremated and turned into a frisbee. That is commitment to the bit.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus. Venus does not do deadlines.
Sharks are older than trees. Let that quietly ruin your afternoon.
A jiffy is a real unit of time: one hundredth of a second. So be there in a jiffy is a bold lie.
Some cats are allergic to humans. Finally, some accountability.
The average cloud weighs about a million pounds. Just floating. No goals. No hustle. Living.
Humans share about 60 percent of their DNA with a banana. So you drive me bananas is mostly self-report.
Nintendo was founded in 1889. It made playing cards before it made plumbers.
Your stomach grows a new lining every few days or it would digest itself. You are, technically, brand new.
Hot water can freeze faster than cold water. It's the Mpemba effect. Physics is just showing off now.
The Eiffel Tower gets about 15 cm taller in summer. Metal expands in heat. It's basically me, growing out of spite.
A snail can sleep for three years. A goal. A dream. A lifestyle I aspire to.
I love mornings. The perfect time to lie down and reconsider mornings.
I'm not lazy. I've simply optimized for stillness.
This meeting could've been an email. The email could've been a text. The text could've been silence.
My hobbies include eating, and then complaining that I ate.
I've been staring at this spreadsheet so long the cells started staring back.
Do I have a five-year plan? I have a five-minute plan and it involves this chair.
Running on three hours of sleep and one heroic cup of coffee. Do not perceive me.
Teamwork makes the dream work. The dream is a nap. Please help me achieve the dream.
I'm not procrastinating. I'm letting the task marinate in avoidance.
Someone microwaved fish. We will find them. We have until three.
The office plant and I are the only ones still here. Neither of us is thriving.
I said let's circle back, then walked in a literal circle. Nobody noticed. I'm free now.
Achievements today: four coffees, zero tasks, one existential moment by the vending machine.
I keep my calendar full so nobody can add more to it. Genius, honestly. Tragic, also.
My out-of-office reply is just active enough to be a little sad.
I told my boss I work well under pressure, then quietly prayed he'd never test it.
I clicked Reply All on purpose once. I felt powerful. I felt free. I got a stern email.
I whispered you got this to the copier. It jammed anyway. Belief, it turns out, is not enough.
Okay so hear me out, what if we completely restructured the— ...you know what? Never mind. Nobody's listening anyway.
I have an absolutely incredible idea and it's going to change every— ...nope. It's gone. You weren't going to care regardless.
Guys. GUYS. This is genuinely important— ...oh. Right. It's just me and the ceiling fan in here again.
The most interesting thing happened this morning and— actually never mind, I can feel your attention leaving already.
Let me just say one thing about the roadmap— okay it left. The thought left. We'll never know now. Tragic.
So the data clearly shows that— ...and now I've lost you. And, frankly, myself. Anyway. Moving on.
Hot take incoming, brace yourselves— no. It fled. Sensed the indifference. Honestly a smart take on its part.
Anyway what I'm really trying to say is— hello? ...cool. Great chat. Loved this. Truly a two-way conversation.
Real quick before you go— oh, you're already gone. In spirit. That's fine. I'm fine. This is fine.
I had a whole point AND a graph to go with it and— nah. Nobody asked. Back in my little box I go.
Does anyone want to hear about— no? ...that's okay. I'll tell the plant. The plant gets me. Mostly.
Shout out to the guy who replies-all to a 400-person thread just to say thanks. A true visionary. Of chaos.
Some people read 'do not reply to this email' as a personal challenge. Icons of not listening.
There is a special confidence in people who are loudly, aggressively wrong. Must be nice up there in the fog.
To whoever microwaves fish in the break room: we don't like you. It's not personal. Okay, it's slightly personal.
Some folks say 'per my last email' when they mean 'as I already said, before you ignored me, you absolute gremlin.'
The person who parks across two spots has told you everything you'll ever need to know about their whole personality.
Ah, the guy who says 'well, actually' and is then, tragically, not actually correct. My favorite genre of person.
Some people hear 'this meeting could've been an email' and schedule a meeting to discuss it. We do not like these people.
Standing ovation for whoever stops dead at the top of the escalator to reconsider their entire life. Perfect spot. No notes.
Certain individuals merge onto the highway at 12 miles an hour and then act shocked. We know who you are. We see you.
The confidence of someone explaining your own job back to you, incorrectly, is a natural wonder. Rude. But a wonder.
To the person who calls it 'just common sense' about the one thing they happen to know: sit down, champ.
Some people skip the turn signal because their next move is a surprise. A gift. For everyone. That nobody asked for.
There's always one guy who takes the last coffee and doesn't start a new pot. History will not be kind to Greg.
The 'I'm not like other people' crowd is, statistically, exactly like other people. The math simply is not on their side.
